messages:
maya: heads-up — during the 09:12 burst we saw sustained p50 ~120ms -> 360ms and p99 spikes to ~1.6s. Warm pool showed 0 available nodes at peak, scale-up finished in ~36s. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~78% to 12%. Posting profiler + logs.

ajit: thanks — pulling profiler now. initial look: kernel-selector logged a bunch of FALLBACK entries for matmul kernels on quantized model v2-q4_0. fallback path is single-threaded GEMM_REF. that explains the CPU-side stall while new GPUs came up.

samir: infra note: one machine in the pool had a non-redwood workload pegging GPU0 at 98% (noisy neighbor). container QoS didn't evict since it was a tolerated workload. saw memory pressure so runtime couldn't place new model instances quickly.

maya: snippets: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] kernel-selector: model=model-x qtype=q4_0 candidate=k210 fallback=GEMM_REF reason=missing_kernel
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kv-cache: hit_rate=0.12 window=60s
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] autoscaler: warm_pool_available=0 desired=4 in_progress=4
```

ajit: also saw batching surge — request_size distribution shifted from 16 tokens median -> 64 tokens, so previous batching heuristic that coalesces small requests under 8ms window started creating very large batches which amplified kernel fallback cost.

samir: `kubectl top pods` snapshot: 
```
node/worker-7 gpu_util=98% nonrw-job
node/worker-9 gpu_util=15% redwood-runtime
```

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaled from 6 -> 12 nodes (started at 09:12:07, finished 09:12:43) :gear:

lindsey: customer-facing note — a few customers reported timeouts around 09:12-09:14. we should have a short message if ETA for mitigation.

ajit: short-term mitigations proposed:
- bump warm_pool_min to 6 and set prewarm_on_spike=true for this model tag
- add a kernel-selector fallback telemetry alert for >5% FALLBACK events in 60s
- limit max_batch_tokens to 128 when fallback detected to avoid giant slow batches

maya: medium-term: prioritize shipping missing optimized kernel (k210) for q4_0 on T4/RTX targets and add precompile step during instance provisioning so instances come up with kernels ready. also consider warm KV-cache seeding for hot prefixes.

infra-sig: we can add a node affinity rule to avoid colocating heavy non-redwood jobs in warm-pool nodes and add eviction policy for noisy tenants. scheduling change can roll in as low-risk patch.

samir: follow-ups: can someone attach full kernel-selector log and the autoscaler timeline? i'll open an incident task.

maya: attaching logs to the thread, created perf-incident-391 in tracker. will follow up with a postmortem once we have the kernel and warm-pool fixes. :thumbsup:

ajit: quick grep output for anyone debugging: 
```
$ grep -A2 "FALLBACK" /var/log/runtime/kernel-selector.log | head -n 20
[09:12:02] FALLBACK model-x q4_0 candidate=k210 -> GEMM_REF
[09:12:02] fallback_reason: missing_kernel_or_gpu_arch_mismatch
[09:12:02] compiled_kernels: [k128,k64]
```

maya: thanks all — main action items captured: increase warm pool, kernel alert, batch cap, noisy-tenant eviction. moving to owner: ajit for kernel alert + precompile, samir for scheduling rule, maya for KV-cache warmup task.

infra-sig: noted, will patch scheduler and schedule a canary rollout tonight.
